-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 1 - HIGH LEVEL
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Words used
  * Leg      = one straight run of path cubes. The runner sticks to the leg's FIRST cube (currentCube) and
               uses that cube's frame for the whole leg: forward = heading, up = TOP face, right = RIGHT face.
  * Face     = 0 TOP, 1 RIGHT, 2 BOTTOM, 3 LEFT. These are relative to the RUNNER: RIGHT = the runner's
               right-hand face when it stands on TOP and looks along the leg.
  * Raw roll = +1 or -1, a 90 degree turn about the heading.
               raw +1 = CLOCKWISE seen from behind the runner:  TOP -> RIGHT -> BOTTOM -> LEFT -> TOP
               raw -1 = COUNTER-CLOCKWISE:                       TOP -> LEFT -> BOTTOM -> RIGHT -> TOP
  * Needed face = the face the runner must be on when it reaches the corner. It is the face pointing
               toward the next leg: next leg turns UP -> TOP, RIGHT -> RIGHT, DOWN -> BOTTOM, LEFT -> LEFT.
               (Planks and the portal door have their own needed faces.)

Inputs (all of them go through the same function, EnqueueTap(-1 = LEFT, +1 = RIGHT)):
  * A / Left arrow / left half of the screen   -> LEFT
  * D / Right arrow / right half of the screen -> RIGHT
  * Touch fires on finger-DOWN (DifficultyProfile fireOnTouchDown = 1). A finger that slides 'swipePixels'
    can turn into a swipe: sideways = left/right, up/down = FLIP (swipeFlip = 1).
  So "left click", "LEFT arrow" and "left tap" are exactly the same thing in this scene.

What a press does in 3.2 (settings: cameraRelativeControls 1, screenAxisControls 1, flipRemapsControls 1,
sideFaceRemap 1, rollMapping Legacy; DifficultyProfile MainScenePropCamera2_Difficulty: fairInput 1,
fairCorners 1, disableFlipRemap 1, doubleTapFlip 1, doubleTapWindow 0.22 s, landingLock 0.03 s,
preCornerBuffer 0.15 s):

  1. The press is queued (max 5 in the queue). It is NOT turned into a face yet.
  2. On the next physics step (FixedUpdate, 50 per second) the press is played. At that moment
     "LEFT/RIGHT" becomes a raw roll (+1/-1) using a sign the game keeps for the leg (legRollSign):
        RIGHT = raw legRollSign,  LEFT = raw -legRollSign.
  3. legRollSign is 0 when the runner lands on a new leg. The FIRST press played on the leg decides it,
     looking at the face the runner is on at that moment:
        a) SCREEN-X rule (used on TOP/BOTTOM faces; with this camera it always wins there):
           work out where a raw +1 roll would land; if that face is clearly left or right on screen
           (|screen x| > 0.15), RIGHT = the roll that lands on the screen-RIGHT face. So on a top or bottom
           face, LEFT always goes to the face drawn on the left of the screen, and RIGHT to the right.
           This holds even when the runner runs TOWARD the camera: then RIGHT goes to the runner's own
           LEFT face, because that face is drawn on the right of the screen.
        b) HEADING rule (used when both possible rolls land at the same screen x. On LEFT/RIGHT faces the
           two choices are TOP and BOTTOM, drawn straight above and below the runner. With the
           45/135/315 degree camera this is |x| = 0.00 every time):
           take the runner's heading as drawn on screen, turn it 90 degrees clockwise ("the runner's
           on-screen right-hand side"), and RIGHT = the roll whose face lies on that side.
  4. The sign is then HELD for the whole leg. A second RIGHT press keeps turning the cube the same way
     round (so RIGHT, RIGHT goes TOP -> RIGHT -> BOTTOM). It does not look at the screen again.
  5. Exception, the SIDE-FACE REMAP (only 3.2 has sideFaceRemap on): once the runner has been on a
     LEFT or RIGHT face for 0.2 s (flipRemapDelay, shrunk by Time.timeScale), and the screen still cannot
     separate TOP from BOTTOM (|x| <= 0.15), the sign is overwritten with +1: RIGHT = the runner's
     right-hand roll (clockwise), LEFT = left-hand roll. When the runner rolls back onto TOP/BOTTOM the
     sign is cleared to 0, so the next press re-decides it with rule 3a.
  6. The top/bottom remap (flipRemapsControls, "swap left/right when on the opposite face") is
     DISABLED in 3.2 by the profile's disableFlipRemap = 1.
  7. If the camera has turned more than 10 degrees by the time the runner lands on a new leg, the mapping
     view is replaced. It is the camera's SETTLED view: where a swing ENDS, not where the camera is
     drawn right now (CameraParentRotator.SettledViewRotation).


-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 2 - THE ALGORITHM IN DETAIL  (PlayerController.cs, class CubeRailRunner)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Press -> queue
  Update():  GetKeyDown(A/LeftArrow) -> EnqueueTap(-1);  GetKeyDown(D/RightArrow) -> EnqueueTap(+1)
  HandleTouchInputFair(): TouchPhase.Began -> EnqueueTap(x > Screen.width/2 ? +1 : -1)
  EnqueueTap(dir):
    - TapIsForNextLeg(): if the queued presses already put the runner on the corner's face AND the corner
      is < 0.15 s away, the press is stored in nextLegBuffer and played right after landing on the next leg.
    - double tap? (see PART 3) -> queue DoubleTapCode (3)
    - else queue dir (-1 / +1)

Queue -> face  (FixedUpdate -> ProcessInputQueue)
  UpdateLegView()      new heading (> 30 deg) => legStartSide = face, legRollSign = 0, sideRemapActive = false,
                       legView = cameraRig.SettledViewRotation if it differs > 10 deg from the old one.
  switchCooldown       0.08 s after a roll (0.03 s after landing), flips skip it.
  ExecuteCode(code)    -1/+1 -> sideBeforeLastTap = face; ChangeSide(code)
  ChangeSide(dir)      dir = ScreenRelativeDir(dir) -> screenAxisControls -> DotProductRollDir(dir)
                       newNormal = AngleAxis(-90 * raw, heading) * currentFaceNormal  -> face index
                       BeginRevolve: 0.10 s arc, cooldown 0.08 s.

DotProductRollDir(screenDir)   (all vectors in the leg's mapping view: camRight, camUp)
  if legRollSign == 0:
      hx = heading . camRight,  hy = heading . camUp
      playerRight = camRight*hy - camUp*hx               // heading turned 90 deg clockwise on screen
      dest = AngleAxis(-90, heading) * faceNormal(current) // where raw +1 lands
      screenX = dest . camRight
      if sideFaceRemap && |screenX| > 0.15 :  legRollSign = sign(screenX)       // SCREEN-X rule
      else                                  :  legRollSign = dest.playerRight >= 0 ? +1 : -1   // HEADING
  return screenDir > 0 ? legRollSign : -legRollSign

UpdateSideFaceRemap()  (FixedUpdate, before the queue)
  on face RIGHT/LEFT, settled flipRemapDelay (0.2 s * min(1, timeScale)):
      xPlus = (AngleAxis(-90, heading) * faceNormal) . camRight
      if |xPlus| <= 0.15 : sideRemapActive = true; legRollSign = +1      // runner's own right-hand roll
  back on TOP/BOTTOM with sideRemapActive : sideRemapActive = false; legRollSign = 0

Which rule is in charge, by face (what the recording showed for every one of the 30 legs):
  On TOP or BOTTOM            -> SCREEN-X decides (|x| = 0.71 every time) => LEFT = screen-left face.
  On LEFT/RIGHT, first 0.2 s  -> HEADING decides (|x| = 0.00) unless a sign is already held.
  On LEFT/RIGHT, after 0.2 s  -> SIDE-FACE REMAP: RIGHT = clockwise (raw +1), LEFT = counter-clockwise.
  After the first played press-> HELD for the rest of the leg (until the side-face remap or a new leg).
  The (camera-swing) "swing" fallback in ScreenRelativeDir never runs in 3.2: DotProductRollDir always
  returns +1/-1.


-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 3 - DOUBLE TAP AND FLIP
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Double tap (EnqueueTap, FairInput path):
  same direction as the last tap AND same leg (lastTapCube == currentCube) AND <= 0.22 s apart
  (unscaled time)  =>  RemoveLastQueued() (drops the first tap if it has NOT played yet), then
  queue DoubleTapCode.  A third tap starts a fresh sequence.
  DoubleTapCode plays as  FlipToOpposite(lastTapExecuted ? sideBeforeLastTap : currentSide):
  => you always end on the face OPPOSITE the one you were on BEFORE the first tap, whichever way the
     first tap rolled. LEFT,LEFT and RIGHT,RIGHT give the same end face.
  Flips skip the cooldown (they play on the next physics step). FlipCooldown 0.10 s, arc 0.12 s.

What really happens (recorded):
  The first tap is always played on the next physics step (<= 0.02 s), long before any human second tap.
  So in practice a double tap is ALWAYS: tap 1 = a normal 90 degree roll, tap 2 = a 90 degree "flip" from
  there to the opposite of the start face, turning the same way round. A single 180 degree flip only
  happens if both taps land inside one 0.02 s physics step. Tested with gaps of 0.04 s and 0.10 s: 7
  double taps, all 7 ended on the correct opposite face, and all played as 90 + 90 (see legs 8, 14,
  16, 17, 18, 23 and 25 in PART 6).
  Two taps further apart than 0.22 s = two separate rolls, using the held sign (still reaches the opposite
  face, unless the side-face remap changed the sign in between - see finding 2).

Flip (up/down swipe, or W/S/Up/Down in Flick mode): queue FlipCode -> FlipToOpposite(current face): one
  180 degree arc. The spin direction comes from the arc maths (SignedAngle, 180 -> +180), not from left/right.
  Not used in this recording (tap mode).

Cube rotation (what the "rot / dRot / top->" columns show):
  The visible cube is VisualWrapper/PivotContainer/CubeMesh (RunnerVisualRig). A roll is a 90 degree vault
  about the heading over 0.10 s: about 1-18 degrees per frame at this editor's frame rate (~400 fps).
  "cw-from-behind" = clockwise seen from behind the runner (= raw +1, the top swings to the runner's
  RIGHT). The second half of a double tap keeps turning the same way.
  At every corner the cube's world rotation jumps 90 degrees in ONE frame ("CORNER re-orient ... snap",
  30 times in 30 legs). The root takes the new leg's heading. Because the cube is symmetric this can't be
  seen unless its skin has a direction.


-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 4 - FINDINGS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Result: 30 legs, 0 deaths, 34 screen taps (7 double taps), 27 rolls, 7 double-tap flips, 0 presses that
landed somewhere other than the face the mapping predicted. The code does what it is written to do.
These are the places where what it does may not match what a player expects:

 1. ON A SIDE FACE, THE SAME PRESS CHANGES MEANING AFTER 0.2 s.
    In the first 0.2 s on a LEFT/RIGHT face the HEADING rule decides. After that the side-face remap sets
    RIGHT = clockwise. The two disagree when (in the mapping view) the runner is on the RIGHT face heading
    screen-left, or on the LEFT face heading screen-right. In this run that was legs 17, 19, 24 and 27.
    Example, leg 17 (heading -X, drawn up-left, camera behind):
        t=23.741 landed on RIGHT:   LEFT -> BOTTOM   RIGHT -> TOP      (HEADING rule)
        t=23.962 0.22 s later:      LEFT -> TOP      RIGHT -> BOTTOM   (SIDE-FACE REMAP)
    A fast player who taps straight after landing gets the opposite of a slower player.

 2. THE REMAP ALSO OVERRIDES A SIGN THE PLAYER HAS ALREADY USED ON THE LEG.
    Example from the first recording (leg 11, heading +Z, camera behind): LEFT on BOTTOM locked RIGHT=raw-1
    and rolled BOTTOM -> LEFT. 0.2 s later on the LEFT face the remap set RIGHT=raw+1. So a second LEFT
    tap (slower than the 0.22 s double-tap window) goes back to BOTTOM, where before 0.2 s it would have
    gone on round to TOP. "LEFT, pause, LEFT" can bounce back instead of going round.

 3. THE HELD SIGN IGNORES THE SCREEN ONCE THE RUNNER IS ROUND THE CUBE.
    After the first roll, the same key keeps turning the cube the same way. On vertical legs and on the
    BOTTOM face this lands on a face drawn on the OTHER side of the screen.
    Frames where LEFT's face is drawn screen-right (or RIGHT's face screen-left), by leg:
        3:504  7:329  8:370  9:365  11:436  14:331  21:301  25:112  28:319  (13/16/18/20: 6-8 frames each)
    Example leg 3 (vertical, up): RIGHT rolled TOP -> RIGHT. Now RIGHT -> BOTTOM, drawn UP-LEFT, and
    LEFT -> TOP, drawn DOWN-RIGHT.
    Example leg 8 (after the double-tap flip to BOTTOM): LEFT -> RIGHT face, drawn DOWN-RIGHT. This
    is because the top/bottom remap is disabled in 3.2 (profile disableFlipRemap = 1).
    No leg in the run needed a press in this state, so it cost nothing here. It matters for a player
    who over-rolls and tries to correct with "the side it is on screen".

 4. THE MAPPING USES THE CAMERA'S END POSITION, NOT WHAT IS ON SCREEN.
    legView = SettledViewRotation (the yaw the camera is swinging TO). Legs 6, 24 and 25 landed during
    camera swings: leg 6 camera at 17 deg, mapping 315; leg 24 camera 338, mapping 135; leg 25 camera 51,
    mapping 135. For the length of the swing, left/right are worked out for a view the player can't see yet.

 5. ON SIDE FACES LEFT/RIGHT GO TO TOP/BOTTOM, WHICH ARE DRAWN STRAIGHT UP/DOWN.
    With the 45/135/315 degree yaws, every LEFT/RIGHT face has both choices at screen x = 0.00. Left/right
    has no screen meaning there, so the HEADING rule, then the remap, decide.

 6. DOUBLE TAP = ROLL + 90 DEGREE FLIP, NEVER ONE 180 DEGREE FLIP (see PART 3). It always ends on the
    correct face. If you want a visible single half-turn, the first tap would have to be held back for a
    few hundredths of a second.


-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 5 - HOW THIS WAS RECORDED / HOW TO READ IT
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  * Tool: Assets/Scripts/LeftRightDebugTxt.cs (dev-only, never saved in a scene). Added at Play time to
    MainScene prop camera 3.2. It plays with real screen taps (CubeRailRunner.SimulateTap = exactly the
    key / touch path). It picks each tap with a side-effect-free copy of DotProductRollDir, so the game
    decides left/right only when a press is PLAYED, as for a human. (HumanSimPlayer would lock it early.)
  * Power diamonds were switched OFF for this play session only, then the run was restarted on a fresh
    path. In the first recording the diamond autopilot rolled the runner by itself (raw rolls, taps
    ignored), which muddied legs 5-8. Nothing was saved to the scene.
  * Bot timing: reacts 0.22 s after landing or after its last tap. Double taps alternate a 0.04 s and a
    0.10 s gap and alternate LEFT,LEFT / RIGHT,RIGHT.
  * Camera mode E (ZoneDrift). The game view ran at ~400 fps in the editor, so a leg is 120-900 lines.
  * Leg 30 is the portal ENTRY runway (needed face = the door face). The recording stops on landing leg 31.

  Leg block (PART 6): heading (world axis + where it points on screen), camera (runner moving AWAY = camera
  BEHIND it, TOWARD = camera IN FRONT of it, SIDEWAYS, VERTICAL; d = heading . camera-forward on the
  ground plane), landed face, needed face and why, the corner's turn (runner-relative) and world/screen
  direction, where each face sits on screen, the leg cube's rotation, LEFT/RIGHT at landing + the rule, the
  mapping changes on the leg, then every event with its frame number.

  Frame line (PART 7):
    f / t          frame number / game time
    leg, cube a/b  leg number, distance along it in cubes / last cube index
    face, need     face now, face needed (corner / plank / portal door)
    heading        world axis + screen direction;  cam = AWAY/TOWARD/SIDEWAYS/VERT + d;  yaw = live camera yaw
    L->X[s] R->Y[s] the face a LEFT / RIGHT press would land on if played now, [s] = where that face is
                   drawn on the live screen (relative to the cube centre)
    sign           legRollSign: +1 = RIGHT is clockwise (raw +1), -1 = RIGHT is counter-clockwise, 0 = not
                   decided yet.  SIDE-REMAP = the side-face remap set it
    rule           held / side-remap(held) / would-decide:SCREEN-X / would-decide:HEADING
    q              queued presses (L, R, DBL = double-tap flip, FLIP), ROLLING = a roll arc is playing
    rot            world euler of the visible cube;  dRot = rotation this frame + what kind;  top-> = where
                   the cube's top is moving on screen
    EVENTS         [driver ...] the bot's decision, TAP:LEFT/RIGHT, <MAPPING ...>, <SIDE-FACE REMAP ...>,
                   ROLL a->b / DOUBLE-TAP FLIP finishing a->b with arc direction + check against prediction

##FRAMES
COLUMNS: f=frame  t=game time  leg=leg no (serial)  face=face the runner is on now  need=face needed for this leg's corner/plank/portal
         cam=runner heading vs camera  L->/R-> = face a LEFT / RIGHT press would land on right now [screen spot of that face]
         rule=what decides it  sign=legRollSign (RIGHT = raw +1 runner's right-hand roll / -1 left-hand, 0 = not decided yet)
         rot=runner cube (visible CubeMesh) world euler  dRot=rotation this frame  top->=where the cube's top is moving on screen

LEG 3  (serial 2, 17 cubes)
  heading      : world +Y(up), screen-UP  (came in by turning UP off the last leg (that leg's frame))
  camera       : climbing straight UP (vertical leg, runs up/down the screen; camera neither behind nor in front); camera yaw 45.0, mapping view yaw 45.0
  landed face  : TOP   needed: RIGHT (corner)  rolls needed 1
  corner       : ends with a turn RIGHT (runner-relative) to world +X, screen-UP-RIGHT -> must be on face RIGHT
  faces on screen (cube centre -> face):  TOP screen-DOWN-RIGHT  RIGHT screen-UP-RIGHT  BOTTOM screen-UP-LEFT  LEFT screen-DOWN-LEFT
